summary: Register-only lookout in Greater Sudbury; no source found gives its build, type, height, staffing or site status.

evidence.supports: Register warns against confusing this tower with the Grassy Lake Fire Tower in Saskatchewan
evidence.quote: This lookout is also known as the 'Grassy Lake Fire Tower', not to be confused with 'Grassy Lake Fire Tower' in Saskatchewan.

evidence.supports: Most Ontario towers erected between the 1920s and the 1950s
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: Towers came under the Department of Lands and Forests, which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: From the 1960s aerial spotting and fire-fighting crews took over the towers' work
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

evidence.supports: Government did not want lawsuits over people hurt climbing unmanned towers
evidence.quote: The government decided that they didn't want any lawsuits on their hands in case careless citizens climbed the unmanned towers and were injured in the process.

evidence.supports: Many towers were destroyed after the decision
evidence.quote: The decision then went through to have many destroyed.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

notes_for_editor: Register-only record: Firelookout.ca gives 'N/A' for elevation, tower type, structure height and year built, and the brief's status and kind are unknown; the location is only 'Greater Sudbury', with coordinates that the register does not explain. Two web searches and one Sudbury News article found nothing on this tower by name. A Mindat entry for a Grassy Lake in Sudbury District turned up in search results, but its page returned HTTP 403 and it sits far from the register's coordinates, so it was not used. The Saskatchewan Grassy Lake Fire Tower is a separate structure and was not researched. Needs a second source (district fire files or a Sudbury historical society) before any build, staffing or status claim. No photos found.
